ANALOGY CANDIDATES: Moving truck vs sports car | 128 GB unified memory is a moving truck — one big shared cargo bay for CPU and GPU instead of a tiny fast trunk (discrete VRAM) | breaks because the truck bay is much slower to load from than HBM: big capacity, lower bandwidth, so huge models fit but generate slowly

Big-block engine that fires fewer cylinders | MoE total params = engine displacement (must fit the garage); active params = cylinders fired per token (sets speed) | breaks because a huge engine still needs the whole garage: total size, not active size, decides whether the model fits in memory at all

Parking a car in a garage by removing seats | quantization = stripping the model down (Q4_K_M = removing seats) so it fits the 128 GB garage | breaks below ~3-bit, where you are cutting structural parts: 'Very low quality' quants fit but the model visibly degrades
MISCONCEPTIONS: 128 GB unified memory can run any ~120B-scale open model | MiniMax-M2 needs 138.59GB even at its recommended Q4_K_M quant, so it misses the 128 GB budget; only 3-bit-class quants like Q3_K_XL (108.74GB) fit | https://huggingface.co/bartowski/MiniMaxAI_MiniMax-M2-GGUF
A 117B-parameter model needs ~240 GB of memory | gpt-oss-120b ships MXFP4-quantized and runs on a single 80GB GPU — roughly 60-70 GB in practice | https://huggingface.co/openai/gpt-oss-120b

If it fits at all, it fits well | GLM-4.5 does squeeze under 128 GB only at 2-bit IQ2_M (115.86GB) rated 'Relatively low quality'; a model that fits at 4-bit or higher is the better buy | https://huggingface.co/bartowski/zai-org_GLM-4.5-GGUF

Bigger total parameter count is always the smarter local pick | The llama.cpp DGX Spark benchmark set pairs a small fast coder (Qwen3 Coder 30B A3B) with bigger reasoners because active params, not total params, set interactive speed | https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions/16578
GLOSSARY: unified memory | A single pool of RAM shared by CPU and GPU (as on DGX Spark GB10), so one big model file needs no splitting between VRAM and system RAM.
quantization (quant) | Compressing model weights to fewer bits per weight (e.g. 4-bit Q4_K_M) to shrink the file and memory footprint at some quality cost.
total vs active parameters | Total parameters are all stored weights and set memory size; active parameters are the weights computed per token and set generation speed.
MoE (Mixture of Experts) | An architecture that stores many expert weight blocks but routes each token through only a few, allowing huge total size with small per-token compute.
GGUF | The llama.cpp ecosystem's single-file model format in which each file is one specific quant of a model, with its size listed in GB on the repo page.
KV cache | Per-conversation memory that grows with context length and must fit in memory alongside the model weights.
MXFP4 | A 4-bit micro-scaling weight format used natively by gpt-oss models and accelerated by Blackwell-class hardware like GB10.
UNVERIFIED: GLM-4.5-Air is widely described as a 106B-total / 12B-active MoE with 128K context and MIT license, but those figures were not stated on any page fetched this session (only its GGUF quant sizes were).
MiniMax-M2 is widely described as a 230B-total / 10B-active MoE with a very long context window, but those figures were not stated on any page fetched this session.
Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B, DeepSeek-V3.x and Kimi K2 are commonly reported as far too large for 128 GB at usable quants, but no fetched page stated their quant file sizes.
Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B appears by name in the llama.cpp DGX Spark benchmark model list, but its GGUF size, context and license were not read from a page this session.
GLM-4.6 exists as a newer GLM coding release, but no page fetched this session states its parameter count or quant sizes, so its 128 GB fit is unknown here.
Devstral is commonly described as a 24B Apache-2.0 coding model that fits easily, but that was not verified on a fetched page this session.
Usable memory on DGX Spark is often reported as ~119-120 GB after system overhead, which would tighten the fits above; not verified on a fetched page this session.
